Iterative proportional scaling ideas go back to Yule (1912) and Kruithof (1937).
Formalized as Iterative Proportional Fitting Procedure (IPFP) by Deming & Stephan (1940).
Known in economics / OR as the RAS method (Bacharach, 1965).
Sinkhorn (1964): first proof of convergence for matrix scaling iterations.
Used in Econ to approximate OT under the name gravity models (Wilson, 1969; Erlander, 1980).
Rebranded as “softassign” (Kosowsky & Yuille, 1994) in assignment problems.
Applied to matching in economics (Galichon & Salanié, 2009), even in ML!
Cuturi (2013): reintroduced entropy-regularized OT to machine learning.
Showed algorithm is efficient, scalable, parallelizable (GPU-friendly).
Produced a differentiable loss → opened door to deep learning applications.
Countless extensions since (symmetry preservation, stochastic versions, etc.).
